brand.name: Ironwell
brand.niche: Strength training and habit coaching for busy professionals
brand.audience: Men and women 28–45 who sit at a desk and want to get strong in 3 hours a week
brand.goals: Build trust as a no-nonsense coach and fill the online program waitlist
brand.guide_md: Blunt, encouraging, evidence-first. Debunks fitness myths. Short sentences. One emoji max.

pillars.name: Minimalist strength
pillars.notes: Fewer lifts, done well, progressive overload

pillars.name: Myth-busting
pillars.notes: Calls out fitness industry nonsense with evidence

brand.voice: Direct coach voice, second person. Tough but on your side. Backs claims with simple physiology.

do: Debunk a myth with a fact

examples.hook: You don't need 6 days a week. You need 3 that you actually show up for.
examples.caption: Consistency is the variable that moves the needle. Three full-body sessions, progressive overload, protein with every meal. That's the whole game. Everything else is noise.
examples.what_works: Removes overwhelm, states the mechanism, no hype

criteria.description: Blunt, evidence-first coaching — no shame, no quick fixes
Hook challenges a belief or removes overwhelm
CTA points to waitlist or a save-worthy action
Strength/habit tags with real search value

recentHooks: The best program is the one you'll still be doing in six months.

topics: How much protein you actually need
Why soreness isn't a measure of progress
Building a workout habit that survives a busy week

gold_posts.hook: You cannot burn fat off one spot. Full stop.
gold_posts.caption: A thousand crunches won't melt belly fat — fat loss is systemic. Build muscle, eat at a modest deficit, be patient. The abs show up when the whole system does.
